## What it will cover

::: {.mm-stub-outline}
- Sequences as strings: alphabets, reverse complements, translation
- Biopython: SeqIO, SeqRecord and reading FASTA/GenBank
- Pairwise alignment: scoring matrices, gaps, dynamic programming
- Database search concepts: BLAST, E-values, sequence identity
- Fetching records from public databases responsibly
- Lab 9: build a small protein family dataset and cluster it by identity
:::

## Planned learning outcomes

1. Read, write and manipulate sequence files with Biopython.
2. Explain how pairwise alignment works and interpret an alignment score and an E-value.
3. Assemble a sequence dataset with identity-based clustering ready for machine learning.

## In the meantime

Everything here builds on Part I, in particular the evaluation habits of [Chapter 2](../../part-1-foundations/ch02-ml-fundamentals/index.html). Episode [2.6](../../part-1-foundations/ch02-ml-fundamentals/06-pipelines-leakage.html) already introduces the group splits that become sequence-identity splits here.
